question: How has our revenue developed month by month over the last year?
paraphrases: Show monthly revenue for the past 12 months
interpretation: Revenue means completed item revenue: SUM(order_items.sale_price) with status 'Complete'. Use the last 12 FULL calendar months and exclude the current partial month, otherwise the last point looks like a false drop. Report orders and average order value next to revenue so growth can be split into volume and basket size.
sql:
SELECT DATE_TRUNC(DATE(oi.created_at), MONTH) AS month,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price), 2) AS completed_revenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders,
  ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(oi.sale_price), COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id)), 2) AS avg_order_value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` AS oi
WHERE oi.status = 'Complete'
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) >= DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 12 MONTH)
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) < DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH)
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
analyst_report:
Summary: completed revenue moved from <first_month_revenue> to <last_month_revenue> over the last 12 complete months.
Drivers: compare order count and average order value; growth driven by orders signals demand, growth driven by AOV signals mix or pricing.
Caveats: current month excluded as incomplete; seasonality is visible only against the same month last year.
Actions: investigate the months with the largest drop; check whether promotions coincide with AOV changes.
